Legend

Status words: confirmed = fixed by the SRS or by k._muz. provisional = set, tuned in playtesting. engineering = a guard or presentation number. superseded = kept for the record, not used. regression = kept because the balance report and test T10 still use it. planned = not built yet.
Files

builds.csv: every chassis x wheels x motor combination, calculated with the Physics Model Specification formulas (unchanged).

simulation.csv: results of the step-by-step simulation in the Physics Model Specification (1/120 s steps; throttle and brake levels read at the end of each step; finish time is the end of the step that reaches the line). Unchanged. Test T10 compares all 135 values.

progression.csv: Knowledge earned and spent (SUPERSEDED).

showcase.csv: the Showcase values.
Formulas used (Physics Model Specification v2)
m = chassis + wheels + motor mass;  R = m g cos(theta) - U (m g on flat dry ground);  rolling friction F_r = mu_r x k_r x R;  grip limit F_lim = mu_g x k_g x R
Max acceleration a = (min(F_d,max, F_lim) - F_r) / m;  max braking deceleration = (min(F_b,max, F_lim) + F_r) / m
Old Mission 1: if top speed is reached first, t = v_max / a + (S - v_max^2 / 2a) / v_max; otherwise t = sqrt(2S / a)
Old Mission 2: ice time t = sqrt(2L / a_ice); coasting distance on sand S = v^2 / (2 mu_r k_r g) with v^2 = 2 a_ice L, so mass and motor cancel
Old Mission 3: brake force builds up linearly over T_b (capped by grip), then stays at full; distance = build-up distance + v^2 / 2a
Notes
Builds sheet times for the old Mission 1 and 2 ignore the throttle build-up; the Simulation sheet includes it (about 0.1-0.5 s more).
g = 9.8 m/s^2 as in the textbook. Question numericals (if questions return) state g = 10 m/s^2.
One rover model, so one maximum brake force for every build.
Spread counts the faster Mission 1 route from the Simulation sheet (17 of 27 builds), as the SRS states. Builds column U uses the closed-form times, which ignore throttle build-up, and shows 18.

The old Mission 3 was on asphalt with the rover towed at 15 m/s and released at the first brake input after the brake line (superseded 2026-10-13 by a drive-in speed trap, itself superseded 2026-10-17). In the regression, stopping distance is measured from 15 m/s with the brake building up from 0 (E21).
Old Mission 2 coasting distance is measured from the rover's position at the end of the step that reaches the power-cut line.
